summary: Add minimized tenant-scoped OIDC session observation, application-level revocation, login evidence and a settings-specific audit view within the existing PostgreSQL, OIDC and asynchronous SIEM boundaries.

impacts.evidence: Session state and evidence are scoped by authenticated organization/workspace claims and forced PostgreSQL RLS.
Only SHA-256 sid/sub references and a bounded client class are stored; raw identifiers, tokens, IP and User-Agent are prohibited; security evidence has a documented 180-day minimum retention.
OpenAPI 0.10.0 adds five settings-security operations and regenerated SDK methods without changing existing operations.
No domain event or canonical envelope changes.
Connector and plugin contracts are unchanged.
Expand migration 000061 creates monotonic session state and append-only login evidence under forced RLS.
Revocation is enforced during authentication and blocks subsequent API access; provider-wide SSO ownership remains with Keycloak.
Session revocation is classified write_sensitive and limited to settings.security.write administrators.
Revocation and audit evidence commit atomically with actor and correlation identifiers; settings audit remains append-only.
No synchronization or reconciliation behavior changes; repeated revocation is a monotonic no-op.
No new outbound destination or synchronous SIEM dependency is introduced.
UI distinguishes configured runtime state from not-verified provider health and observed sessions from provider login history.
Deployment requires migration 000061 first; evidence tables are retained through rollback and retention policy.
API privacy/revocation tests, migration invariants, route parity, SDK generation and frontend type checks cover the change.
